title: The Songbook of Maple Hollow
premise: Vesper Underhill has built a career on other people's voices, and her newest contract is the cruelest yet: ghostwriting the memoir of Alden Frost, the rival songwriter who once broke her heart—and who doesn't know she's behind his ghost. When a snowstorm traps them both in Maple Hollow, Vermont, at the inn where they spent one perfect week in their twenties, old songs and older wounds resurface. As Vesper writes Alden's life in secret, she realizes he's been writing about her all along, and that his memoir's final chapter will expose—or erase—her forever. She must choose between the safety of invisibility and claiming authorship of her own story, even if it costs her the man, the book deal, and the only belonging she's ever found.
about_author: Jonah Delacroix is a former small-town radio host who spent a decade writing love letters for strangers before turning to fiction. He lives off-season in a shuttered Vermont inn, where he claims every song sounds better out of tune.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In Brooklyn, Vesper signs a lucrative contract to ghostwrite a memoir—then learns the author is Alden Frost, the songwriter she loved and left fifteen years ago. She almost walks away, but her bank account and her pride make the decision for her. Beat: dread disguised as ambition.

chapters.title: Contract Terms
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. First interview session via video call; Alden is polished, guarded, and cruelly charming. He dictates a chapter about 'a girl who could hear what songs wanted to be,' and Vesper types it with shaking hands. Beat: the past arrives as homework.

chapters.title: Maple Hollow, Off Season
chapters.summary: Alden's POV. Alden travels to Maple Hollow to record oral-history material at the Hollow Inn, unaware his ghost will be there. He remembers the week he and Vesper wrote three songs in this very parlor—and why she vanished. Beat: nostalgia sharpened into grievance.

chapters.title: Snowbound
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The storm hits early; roads close; the innkeeper, Ruthie, recognizes them both and says nothing—but smiles too knowingly. Vesper and Alden come face to face over the check-in desk. Beat: collision, masked as civility.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating scenes. They negotiate an armed truce: professional interviews by day, separate wings by night. Ruthie enforces communal dinners. A power outage forces candlelight and the first real conversation in fifteen years. Beat: wary thaw.

chapters.title: The Songbook
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Ruthie produces the inn's old guest songbook—their three unfinished songs still inside, in two handwritings. Alden sees Vesper's handwriting and goes quiet. Neither names what happened. Beat: evidence of intimacy neither can deny.

chapters.title: Interview, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Alden's POV. The first formal memoir session collapses when Alden asks why she left without goodbye. Vesper answers with a truth half-true: she was nobody, and he was already signed. He calls it a lie. Beat: wound reopened, blame assigned.

chapters.title: What Ruthie Knows
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV (brief interlude). The innkeeper reveals—in thought and a phone call—that Vesper's late mother once sang here, that the inn itself is being sold, and that Ruthie has kept Vesper's mother's demo tape for twenty years. Beat: inheritance foreshadowed.

chapters.title: Second Verse
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Snowed in another day, they finish one of the old songs at the piano, hands nearly touching. For an hour it's their twenties again. Then Alden mentions his fiancée back in Nashville—a PR engagement. Beat: hope punished.

chapters.title: The Rival's Version
chapters.summary: Alden's POV. Dictating his memoir honestly for the first time, Alden describes the night Vesper left—and admits he never sent the letter he wrote her. Vesper, transcribing, realizes they were both cowards, not betrayers. Beat: mutual absolution, unspoken.

chapters.title: Lending Pieces
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Her editor calls: the memoir needs a climactic 'great lost love' chapter, and Alden has authorized using real names—including hers. Vesper must write her own heartbreak as someone else's property. Beat: invisibility becomes unbearable.

chapters.title: The Demo Tape
chapters.summary: Ruthie plays Vesper's mother's tape in the empty kitchen. Vesper hears her own melody in her mother's hummed chorus—the song she's been chasing her whole life was inherited, not invented. Beat: grief transmuted into belonging.

chapters.title: Thaw Line
chapters.summary: Alden's POV. Roads partially clear; Alden could leave but delays his departure, lying to his manager. He and Vesper walk the frozen hollow, and he tells her about the unsent letter. She tells him about the ghostwriting—of other books, not his. Yet. Beat: confession in installments.

chapters.title: Chapter Seventeen
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Writing his 'lost love' chapter, Vesper inserts the true ending—the letter, the tape, the inn—and submits it, knowing Alden reads every draft. It's a message smuggled through enemy lines. Beat: authorship as courage.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Alden's POV. Alden reads the draft alone at 3 a.m., recognizing himself more clearly than he ever has. He confronts Vesper—not with anger but with the question he should have asked at twenty-three: 'Was any of it mine?' Beat: vulnerability as climax approach.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper confesses everything: she is the ghost, she has been all along, and the memoir's best pages are thefts from her own heart. Alden's face closes. He leaves for the airport as the last snowplow passes. Beat: the whole heart risked and seemingly lost.

chapters.title: Nashville Interlude
chapters.summary: Alden's POV. Back home, Alden ends the engagement honestly, then rereads the manuscript and finds what Vesper hid in the acknowledgments page: her mother's name, and the words 'for the one who stayed.' Beat: realization and reversal.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV. The inn's foreclosure auction is announced; Ruthie is losing Maple Hollow. Vesper returns—not for Alden, but to bid with her entire advance, publicly claiming her mother's legacy and her own name for the first time. Beat: justice outside the law, paid in full.

chapters.title: Unsent, Delivered
chapters.summary: Alden's POV. Alden arrives mid-auction with the fifteen-year-old letter, yellowed and sealed, and reads it aloud in front of the town. The letter ends with the melody of their finished song. Vesper bids her last dollar; Alden bids the letter's royalties. Together they win the inn. Beat: public reckoning, private vow.

chapters.title: Co-Authorship
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Negotiations with the publisher: the memoir will carry dual credit—his name, hers beneath it, no longer invisible. Alden insists the lost-love chapter stay exactly as she wrote it. Beat: inheritance claimed, identity restored.

chapters.title: The Songbook of Maple Hollow
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs converging. Spring opening of the inn as a writers' retreat; the guest songbook gets new entries in two familiar handwritings. Ruthie stays on as keeper. The final scene mirrors their first meeting at the check-in desk—except this time, no one checks out. Beat: belonging earned.

chapters.title: Coda: What Songs Want
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, years later. A young ghostwriter arrives at the inn, terrified and talented, and Vesper hands her the old songbook with the same advice her mother's tape gave her: lend nothing you can't afford to lose, and sign everything. Beat: quiet, complete resolution.
